headline: US stocks suffered their worst day since 2025 on 5 Nov as chip shares plunged. Hormuz stays largely shut with more tankers hit, Russia keeps striking Ukraine's grid, and DR Congo's Ebola outbreak passed 10,600 cases.

situations.name: US–Iran war and Gulf energy shock
situations.summary: Iran says more tankers hit mines in Hormuz on 5 Nov; US officials say forces are poised to resume major combat. Brent near $99.

situations.name: Russia–Ukraine war and NATO's flank
situations.summary: Russia launched 128 drones overnight into 5 Nov after mass grid strikes; NATO commander warns Poland of border provocations.

situations.name: Super El Niño
situations.summary: ONI rose to +2.5 for Aug–Oct: drought risk in East and southern Africa, record-range warmth and faster CO₂ growth.

situations.name: Ebola outbreak, DR Congo
situations.summary: ECDC counted 10,668 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,198 deaths in DR Congo to 3 Nov; cases in Kenya; a WHO PHEIC since May.

situations.name: Sudan war
situations.summary: UN warns of deadly drone strikes on Sudan's grid and civilians; a South Kordofan fuel-station strike killed at least 7 on 4 Nov.

situations.name: France: debt stress and protests
situations.summary: OAT–Bund spread near 160bp; nationwide strike on 5 Nov with largely peaceful marches; budget deadline 17 Nov.

situations.name: Energy shock feeding inflation
situations.summary: Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023; traders add to bets on a December hike.

situations.name: Binance theft and North Korean escalation
situations.summary: FBI blames North Korea for a $6.3bn Binance theft; Pyongyang denied it and fired several missiles on 4 Nov. Binance withdrawals have resumed.

signals.name: US equity stress
signals.summary: S&P 500 falls 4.3% on 5 Nov, its worst day since 2025, as chip stocks plunge; VIX 28
signals.state: The S&P 500 fell about 4.3% on 5 Nov and the Nasdaq 5.5%, closing in correction, as the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped 12% (Yahoo Finance). The S&P is 6.0% below its 52-week high and the VIX closed at 28.2, both inside the Watch band and below the VIX 30 Alert line. October payrolls are due on 6 Nov.
signals.for_you: Sharp equity falls hit pension and investment values in the short term; volatility often stays high for days after a move this size.
signals.rubric_hit: VIX 28.2 in 20–30 band; S&P drawdown 6.0% in 5–15% Watch band

Yahoo Finance — ^VIX

signals.name: FTSE 100
signals.summary: FTSE 100 near 10,783 on 5 Nov, 1.2% below its high, despite the US sell-off
signals.state: The FTSE 100 closed near 10,783 on 5 Nov, 1.2% below its 52-week high and 0.5% higher on the week (Yahoo Finance). Its worst day in the past five sessions was a 1.1% fall, well inside the 5% drawdown and 2.5% daily-fall Watch lines, even as US stocks fell over 4% on 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: UK shares have held up so far; a steep US sell-off can still spill into London trading in the following sessions.
signals.rubric_hit: FTSE drawdown 1.2% < 5%; worst day −1.1% > −2.5%

signals.name: Bond market volatility
signals.summary: MOVE index near 98 and US 10-year yield 4.84%, both at the edge of the Watch lines
signals.state: The MOVE index of Treasury volatility was about 98 on 5 Nov and the US 10-year yield 4.84%, about 39bp lower than a month earlier (Yahoo Finance). Both readings sit just under the Watch lines (MOVE 100, 40bp a month), so Watch is kept until they clearly clear them. October payrolls on 6 Nov are the next test.
signals.for_you: Swings in US yields feed through to mortgage and borrowing costs worldwide, including fixed-rate deals in the UK.
signals.rubric_hit: MOVE 98 and 10y 1m move 39bp at the Watch lines (100, 40bp)

signals.summary: US high-yield spreads 3.32%, inside the 4% Watch line

signals.for_you: Corporate borrowing costs remain contained; wider spreads would signal tighter credit for riskier firms.

signals.for_you: A large fall in gold signals a shift in how markets price safety; it says little on its own about near-term risk.

signals.summary: Bitcoin near $75,500, 13% off its high; no stablecoin de-peg
signals.state: Bitcoin was near $75,500 early on 6 Nov, 12.8% below its 52-week high and 3.5% lower on the week, inside the 25% Watch line (Yahoo Finance). No stablecoin de-peg or exchange failure had been reported as of 6 Nov.
signals.for_you: Crypto prices remain volatile; holders are exposed to sharp swings, especially when equities sell off.

signals.name: Dollar funding stress
signals.summary: SOFR peaked 7bp above the reserve rate; Fed repo use near zero
signals.state: SOFR was 4bp above the Fed's interest on reserves on 4 Nov and peaked at 7bp over five days, inside the 10bp Watch line; Fed overnight repo operations were zero to 5 Nov (FRED). Money markets show no sign of a dollar shortage as of 6 Nov.
signals.for_you: Short-term funding markets are calm; strain here would usually show up before wider credit problems.
signals.rubric_hit: SOFR–IORB 5d max 7bp < 10bp; repo $0bn < $15bn

signals.name: Private credit stress
signals.summary: Non-traded BDC redemption requests still exceed quarterly caps; no forced sales or bank spillover
signals.state: Redemption requests at non-traded BDCs, including Blackstone's BCRED, have run well above the usual 5% quarterly caps, and requests now exceed new fundraising (InvestmentNews; Bloomberg Government). Gates remain in force at several funds. No forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers had been reported as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may face limits on withdrawals; borrowers reliant on private lenders may find credit tighter.
signals.rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions = Watch; no multi-fund gating with forced sales

signals.for_you: The yen is stable; a sudden jump would signal leveraged positions being unwound across markets.

signals.name: US inflation
signals.summary: US CPI 4.0% y/y in September; October data due 10 Nov
signals.state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7%, inside the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). Brent rebounded on 5 Nov from a two-month low near $94 as uncertainty over the Iran war persisted (The National), so energy prices remain a risk to the October figure, due on 10 Nov.
signals.for_you: Higher prices for fuel, food and services squeeze household budgets; mortgage and loan rates tend to stay high while inflation is above target.
signals.rubric_hit: CPI 4.0% within 3.0–4.5% Watch band

signals.name: Euro-area economy
signals.summary: Euro-area composite PMI 51.9 in October; Q3 GDP grew 0.4%
signals.state: The HCOB euro-area flash composite PMI fell to 51.9 in October, below the 52.7 expected but above 50 (FXStreet, 23 Oct). Eurostat's flash estimate showed Q3 GDP up 0.4%. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 PMI had been reported as of 5 Nov, so the Normal criteria still hold.
signals.for_you: Euro-area growth is positive but slowing; exporters and jobs in energy-heavy industries remain most exposed.
signals.rubric_hit: GDP +0.4% and composite PMI 51.9 > 50 = Normal

signals.name: China economy
signals.summary: China services growth slows to 50.8 in October; factory PMI in contraction
signals.state: China's Caixin services PMI eased to 50.8 in October, a three-month low, as confidence weakened (Yahoo Finance; investingLive, 4 Nov). The official manufacturing PMI was 49.3 and regulators paused IPOs to steady stocks in early November. Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, near target, with no sign of financial contagion as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Slower Chinese demand weighs on commodity exporters and firms selling into China; no acute disruption is reported.
signals.rubric_hit: Growth near target, no contagion = Normal

signals.name: Central bank stress
signals.summary: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov and warns inflation will near 5%
signals.state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, and warned inflation will approach 5% as the energy shock feeds through (CNBC; Bank of England). Australia's central bank hiked to 4.85% on 3 Nov, and the ECB and Bank of Japan held in late October. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency move has been made.
signals.for_you: Borrowing costs are rising again in several economies; variable-rate mortgages and new loans are most exposed.
signals.rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma at major central banks = Watch; no emergency moves

Bank of England — Interest rates and Bank Rate

signals.summary: France–Bund spread near 160bp, above the 150bp Alert line, as unions strike on 5 Nov
signals.state: France's 10-year spread over German Bunds was reported near 160bp in the week to 5 Nov, above the 150bp Alert line, as the 2027 budget vote slipped toward a 17 Nov deadline (Journal du Coin; Trading Economics). Unions held a nationwide strike on 5 Nov (Al Jazeera). No failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying has been reported.
signals.for_you: Higher French borrowing costs can feed through to euro-area mortgage and corporate rates; this describes market conditions only.
signals.rubric_hit: France–Bund ~160bp > 150bp Alert line

signals.state: The J.P.Morgan Global Manufacturing PMI eased to 52.6 in October from 53.0, still well above 50 (S&P Global). The global composite was at its joint-highest since 2021 in September; the October composite had not been found as of 5 Nov. No reading near the 51 Watch line has been reported.
signals.for_you: Global factory activity is still expanding; no broad downturn is signalled for trade-exposed jobs.

signals.state: Initial US jobless claims were 189,000 in the week to 31 Oct, pulling the four-week average down to about 194,750, its 52-week low and far from the 15% Watch line (Department of Labor via FRED). Layoffs remain low as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Layoffs remain low, so job security for most US workers is not under new pressure.
signals.rubric_hit: 4wk avg 0% above 52w low < 15% = Normal

signals.name: Emerging-market stress
signals.value: Lira past 50/$; EGP at record low
signals.summary: Turkish lira breaches 50 per dollar; no major EM default or capital controls
signals.state: The Turkish lira broke through 50 per dollar to a record low on 4 Nov, extending a gradual slide (Shafaq News; Trading Economics). Egypt's pound has also hit record lows. Neither has lost more than 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy had defaulted, imposed capital controls or sought emergency IMF help as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Weaker currencies raise import costs in Turkey and Egypt; travellers and exporters see changing exchange rates.
signals.rubric_hit: No major EM >10% monthly fall, default or controls = Normal

Alert is kept on the physical outage: Hormuz remains largely shut, UKMTO counted 35 vessels hit in October, the most of the war, and Iran reported three more tankers damaged on 5 Nov (Nation Thailand).
signals.for_you: Fuel, heating and transport costs stay exposed to Gulf supply; prices can move sharply on news from Hormuz.

signals.value: Hormuz largely shut; 3 tankers hit 5 Nov
signals.summary: Iran says three tankers hit mines and caught fire in Hormuz on 5 Nov; 35 vessels hit in October
signals.state: Iran's forces said a tanker caught fire after striking a mine in Hormuz on 5 Nov and that three more hit mines, and UKMTO reported a tanker hit by two projectiles north of Qatar late on 4 Nov (Al Jazeera). UKMTO counted 35 vessels hit in October, the most of the war (Nation Thailand). Traffic remains materially impeded, meeting the Alert line.
signals.for_you: Shipping delays and higher freight and insurance costs feed through to energy and goods prices. Mariners should follow UKMTO advisories.

signals.state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls, including the 0.1% content rule, expires on 10 Nov, and no renewal had been announced as of 5 Nov (Yahoo Finance; Technology.org). signals.summary: Gulf urea exports still stuck behind a largely closed Hormuz; tankers hit on 5 Nov
signals.state: Hormuz, a route for about a third of world urea exports, remains largely closed in the conflict's ninth month, keeping fertiliser costs high (Global Agriculture; European Commission). Tankers were hit in the strait again on 5 Nov (US News). A key export route closed meets the Alert line.
signals.for_you: Farmers face higher input costs, which can feed into food prices next season.
signals.rubric_hit: Key export route (Hormuz) closed = Alert

signals.name: Nuclear plant safety
signals.summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on a single power line as Russian strikes hit Ukraine's grid
signals.state: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has relied on a single off-site line since repairs agreed under an IAEA-brokered local ceasefire (Arms Control Association). Russian strikes continued to hit Ukraine's energy system into 5 Nov (Forbes). No damage to safety systems or radiological release has been reported.
signals.for_you: No public health action is advised; follow IAEA and national regulator updates.
signals.rubric_hit: Plant on minimal off-site power amid grid strikes = Watch

signals.name: US–China / Taiwan
signals.summary: 49 PLA aircraft around Taiwan on 3 Nov, one of the busiest days of 2026; no exercise announced
signals.state: Taiwan's defence ministry reported 49 Chinese military aircraft, 31 of them inside its air defence zone, plus six warships and six official ships in the 24 hours to 3 Nov (Storm Media). Analysts call it an unannounced 'quiet exercise'; China has held no named drill since December 2025. Taiwan's local elections are on 28 Nov. Normal holds until a declared large-scale drill or incident.
signals.for_you: No direct effect for most people; a declared exercise or blockade would disrupt shipping and chip supply chains.
signals.rubric_hit: Routine-to-elevated PLA activity; no large-scale declared exercise

signals.name: Russia–NATO
signals.summary: NATO commander warns Poland of possible Russian provocations on its north-east border
signals.state: Polish PM Donald Tusk said on 3 Nov that NATO's top commander, Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, had warned of possible Russian provocations on Poland's north-eastern border; Poland deployed extra police and border units on 2 Nov and guards reported suspicious activity near Sępopol late on 3 Nov (Stars and Stripes; CBS News). No NATO member had requested Article 4 consultations as of 6 Nov.
signals.for_you: No change for the public; follow official guidance if travelling near Poland's border with Kaliningrad.
signals.rubric_hit: Explicit threats and border provocations; no Article 4 or clash

signals.name: Iran nuclear programme
signals.summary: No IAEA access to key Iranian sites; US strikes so far hit military, not nuclear, targets
signals.state: The IAEA has had no access to key Iranian sites since the war began. US strikes on 3 Nov hit an air-defence site on Qeshm Island, not nuclear facilities (Stars and Stripes), and Iran called the US reply to its Hormuz plan unconvincing on 4 Nov (Al Jazeera). Searches on 6 Nov found no strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or new IAEA report.
signals.for_you: No direct public effect; a strike on nuclear sites would sharply raise regional and energy-market risk.
signals.rubric_hit: Inspector access curtailed + credible strike threats = Watch

signals.value: Missile salvo 4 Nov; 4th launch in a month
signals.summary: North Korea fired several missiles on 4 Nov, its fourth launch in a month
signals.state: North Korea fired several missiles toward the Sea of Japan on 4 Nov, its fourth weapons launch in a month, South Korea's military said (US News; Japan Times). State media said an earlier weekend launch tested a new dispersion warhead. No nuclear test or ICBM overflight of Japan had been reported as of 6 Nov.
signals.for_you: No direct effect outside the region; Japan and South Korea issue alerts to residents if a launch threatens their territory.
signals.rubric_hit: Ballistic missile launches = Watch; no nuclear test or overflight

signals.state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls, including the 0.1% content rule, expires on 10 Nov, and no renewal had been announced as of 6 Nov (Technology.org; Startup Fortune). signals.state: The US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in force, and Iran's terms for a deal include an end to it and sanctions relief; Tehran contacted Oman, Qatar and Saudi Arabia on 5 Nov amid fears of new US strikes (Al Jazeera). signals.state: False bomb threats affected at least 17 flights across Europe on 5 Nov after similar hoaxes earlier in the week; no explosives were found (ABC News Australia). Bulgaria reported three emergency landings and Czech police rated threats to Prague-bound flights as low credibility (The National). Remote attacks on supermarket refrigeration hit EU stores on 2 Nov. No state has been formally blamed.
signals.for_you: Expect occasional diversions and delays on European flights; follow airline and airport advice.

signals.name: Russia–Ukraine
signals.summary: Russia keeps up mass drone strikes on Ukraine's grid; Ukraine hits Russian refineries
signals.state: Russia launched 128 drones and two missiles overnight into 5 Nov, killing a woman in Sumy region (Kyiv Post), a day after a 310-drone attack that followed a mass strike on the power grid on 3 Nov (The Defense Post). Zelensky said on 1 Nov that attacks on energy in four regions left hundreds of thousands of families without power (Ukrainska Pravda). The 3 Nov aid-centre strike was among the war's deadliest.
signals.for_you: Follow FCDO travel advice: it advises against all travel to Ukraine.

signals.name: UK inflation & rates
signals.summary: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov; warns inflation will near 5%
signals.state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, reversing its easing cycle, and warned inflation will approach 5% (CNBC; Bank of England). UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in September, inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band.
signals.for_you: Variable and tracker mortgages, and new fixed deals, are likely to cost more; savings rates may rise.
signals.rubric_hit: BoE reversing course and CPI 3.5% = Watch
signals.basis_detail: ONS CPI and Bank of England decisions
signals.basis_by: ONS CPI and Bank of England decisions

sources.title: Bank of England — Interest rates and Bank Rate

signals.name: Gilt market
signals.summary: Gilt yields rise after the Bank of England's first rate rise since 2023 on 5 Nov
signals.state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov on an 8–1 vote, its first rise in three years, and gilt yields rose, led by two-year bonds (Euronext); traders added to bets on a December hike (Bloomberg). The 10-year yield had fallen to 5.14% on 4 Nov, a two-month low and below its mid-October multi-year high (Trading Economics). No weak auction or BoE intervention has been reported.
signals.for_you: Higher gilt yields feed through to fixed-rate mortgage pricing and government borrowing costs.
signals.rubric_hit: Long gilts near multi-decade highs = Watch; 10y 1m move < 40bp

sources.title: Euronext — Bank of England delivers first rate hike in three years, gilt yields rise

signals.name: UK energy price cap
signals.summary: Energy cap £1,723; final January forecasts point to the highest cap since January 2024
signals.state: The Ofgem cap for October–December is £1,723 a year. Cornwall Insight has released its final January forecast, and reports say the cap will rise to its highest since January 2024; its earlier forecast was £1,999, up 16% (Cornwall Insight; Hargreaves Lansdown). Alert is held under hysteresis until Ofgem announces the January cap by 25 Nov.
signals.for_you: Households on standard variable tariffs should expect higher bills from January; Ofgem and Citizens Advice list support schemes.
signals.rubric_hit: Forecast rise ≥ 5%; Alert held pending Ofgem's 25 Nov announcement

signals.name: NHS & respiratory
signals.summary: UKHSA publishes 5 Nov flu report; flu low but rising; doctors strike 14–19 Nov
signals.state: UKHSA's 29 Oct report showed flu activity low but GP swab positivity rising to 11.0%, COVID low and falling and RSV at baseline; its next report, covering data to 1 Nov, was published on 5 Nov (UKHSA). Resident doctors in England strike from 14 to 19 Nov (BMA). No widespread critical incidents have been reported.
signals.for_you: Eligible people can book flu and COVID-19 vaccines through the NHS; use NHS 111 for non-emergency advice.
signals.rubric_hit: Respiratory activity near baseline, no widespread critical incidents = Normal

signals.name: UK terrorism threat level
signals.summary: UK national threat level Severe: an attack is highly likely
signals.state: The UK national terrorism threat level has been Severe, meaning an attack is highly likely, since JTAC raised it from Substantial on 30 Apr 2026 (MI5). No change had been announced as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Follow MI5 and police guidance on staying alert in crowded places; report concerns to the police.
signals.rubric_hit: MI5 level Severe = Alert

sources.title: MI5 — Threat levels

signals.name: UK strikes & disruption
signals.summary: Resident doctors strike 14–19 Nov; consultants 25–26 Nov
signals.state: The BMA has called a six-day strike by resident doctors in England from 14 to 19 Nov, and consultants will strike on 25–26 Nov (BMA; IBTimes UK). These are strikes in one sector, within the Watch band. No national infrastructure failure had been reported as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: Keep NHS appointments unless told otherwise; use NHS 111 or 999 as normal during strikes.
signals.rubric_hit: National strike in one sector = Watch

signals.name: GB energy supply margins
signals.summary: NESO expects adequate electricity margins this winter; no notices issued
signals.state: NESO's winter outlook expects adequate GB electricity margins, which it called the strongest in six years, though some analysts see a lower buffer (NESO; Drax). No Electricity Margin Notice, capacity market notice or Gas Margins Notice had been issued as of 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: No action needed; NESO publishes notices if margins tighten.
signals.rubric_hit: No NESO or National Gas notices = Normal
